questions.scenario:
The descriptions below are of four cells, each in a different phase of mitosis.
Cell 1: the chromosomes are lined up on the equator, attached to spindle fibres by their centromeres.
Cell 2: the chromatids are pulled to opposite poles.
Cell 3: the nuclear membrane disappears and the chromosomes shorten, thicken and become visible.
Cell 4: a nuclear membrane forms around each group of chromosomes and the cytoplasm starts to divide.
questions.scenarioAf:
Die beskrywings hieronder is van vier selle, elk in ’n ander fase van mitose.
Sel 1: die chromosome is op die ewenaar in lyn, deur hul sentromere aan spoelvesels geheg.
Sel 2: die chromatiede word na teenoorgestelde pole getrek.
Sel 3: die kernmembraan verdwyn en die chromosome word korter, dikker en sigbaar.
Sel 4: ’n kernmembraan vorm om elke groep chromosome en die sitoplasma begin verdeel.

pointsAf: Sel 1: metafase

questions.q:
Describe how water moves from the soil into a plant and up to the leaves, and explain how the structure of xylem vessels suits them for transporting water.
Content: 17 Synthesis: 3
NOTE: NO marks will be awarded for answers in the form of flow charts, tables or diagrams.
questions.qAf:
Beskryf hoe water van die grond af ’n plant binnegaan en tot by die blare beweeg, en verduidelik hoe die struktuur van xileemvate hulle geskik maak om water te vervoer.
Inhoud: 17 Sintese: 3
LET WEL: GEEN punte sal toegeken word vir antwoorde in die vorm van vloeidiagramme, tabelle of diagramme nie.
points: Root hairs give a large surface area for absorbing water
Soil water is more dilute than the cell sap of the root hair
so water enters the root hair by osmosis
Water moves from cell to cell across the cortex by osmosis
It passes through the endodermis into the xylem
Root pressure pushes water a short way up the xylem
In the stem, water moves up in the xylem as a continuous column
Transpiration pull: water lost from the leaves pulls the column of water upwards
Cohesion: water molecules are attracted to each other
Adhesion: water molecules are attracted to the xylem walls
Capillarity in the narrow xylem vessels helps water to rise
In the leaf, water moves from the xylem into the mesophyll cells by osmosis
It evaporates into the air spaces
and diffuses out through the stomata (transpiration)
Xylem vessels are dead cells with no cytoplasm, so water flows freely
The end walls have broken down, forming continuous tubes
The walls are thickened with lignin, which gives strength and stops the vessels from collapsing
Pits in the walls allow water to move sideways between vessels
The narrow lumen helps capillarity
pointsAf: Wortelhare gee ’n groot oppervlakte vir die absorpsie van water
Grondwater is meer verdun as die selsap van die wortelhaar
dus gaan water die wortelhaar deur osmose binne
Water beweeg deur osmose van sel tot sel oor die korteks
Dit gaan deur die endodermis na die xileem
Worteldruk stoot water ’n entjie teen die xileem op
In die stingel beweeg water as ’n aaneenlopende kolom in die xileem op
Transpirasietrek: water wat uit die blare verlore gaan, trek die waterkolom opwaarts
Kohesie: watermolekules word na mekaar aangetrek
Adhesie: watermolekules word na die xileemwande aangetrek
Kapillariteit in die nou xileemvate help water om te styg
In die blaar beweeg water deur osmose van die xileem na die mesofilselle
Dit verdamp in die lugruimtes in
en diffundeer deur die huidmondjies uit (transpirasie)
Xileemvate is dooie selle sonder sitoplasma, dus vloei water vrylik
Die eindwande het afgebreek en vorm aaneenlopende buise
Die wande is met lignien verdik, wat sterkte gee en keer dat die vate inmekaarval
Putte in die wande laat water sywaarts tussen vate beweeg
Die nou lumen help kapillariteit

points: Relevance (1): all the information is about water movement and xylem structure; nothing irrelevant
Logical sequence (1): soil → root → stem → leaf in a logical order
Comprehensive (1): at least 9/14 for water movement and 3/5 for xylem structure
pointsAf: Relevansie (1): al die inligting gaan oor waterbeweging en xileemstruktuur; niks irrelevant nie
Logiese volgorde (1): grond → wortel → stingel → blaar in ’n logiese volgorde
Omvattend (1): ten minste 9/14 vir waterbeweging en 3/5 vir xileemstruktuur
